rationale: A wins because it turns the supplied holes into story discipline: "24,000 paid teams, 220 million users — and Canva can't name one enterprise customer" is skeptical, reportable, and honest about what still needs proving. B has real scaffolding, but "Canva has converted just 24,000 of its 220 million users into paying teams" botches the metric by comparing users to teams and then builds a funnel story on sand. A still overreaches on the acquisition-to-product link, but it usually labels the missing proof instead of laundering guesses into facts.
gaps_in_A: "Canva bought an AI image startup, then shipped it as a brand-safety feature" asserts a causal product link the update does not give. The proof note admits the hole, but the headline already crossed the line.
"the exact moat Adobe has used to hold enterprise accounts" may be true, but it is not in the supplied update. Say it needs reporting; do not smuggle it in as settled market analysis.
"Canva can't name one enterprise customer" is sharper than the facts. The update says named enterprise customers were not disclosed, not that Canva cannot name one.

"Design tools are becoming compliance software" is a good trend frame, but it leans hard on SSO/admin controls before proving actual compliance features like audit logs, SCIM, data residency, or retention.
gaps_in_B: "Canva has converted just 24,000 of its 220 million users into paying teams" is the worst miss. Users and teams are different units; that is not a conversion rate, it is arithmetic wearing a fake mustache.
"Canva finally builds the SSO and admin controls IT departments were blocking it for" invents prior IT blockage. The update says the features launched, not that blockers existed or were cleared.

"How a $26 billion private company keeps expanding without touching public markets" drifts into finance fan fiction. Private, profitable, and valued at $26B do not prove the enterprise push or acquisition were funded by profit, nor that public markets were a live alternative.

"Canva bought its way into proprietary AI capability rather than bolting on a general-purpose model" is not grounded in the update. The acquisition exists; the technology path and model strategy do not.
